newsitem.title: USA: Morton shareholders approve spinoff, deal.
newsitem.headline: Morton shareholders approve spinoff, deal.

text.p: Morton International Inc said Thursday its shareholders approved the spinoff of Morton's specialty chemicals and salt businesses and the combination of Morton's airbag business with Autoliv AB to create Autoliv Inc.
The board of directors set the close of business April 30 conditionally as the record date and distribution date for the dividend to be paid to Morton shareholders.

Following the completion of the spinoff, Morton authorized the initial repurchase of up to 10 million share of the company's common stock. Morton said its management will decide whether to buy some or all under a Dutch tender offer or to buy the shares on the open market.
The dividend consists of one share of the common stock as well as a related preferred share purchase right of "new" Morton International for each share of Morton common held.
The Morton board conditionally declared the close of business on April 30, 1997 as the record date and the distribution date for the dividend to be paid to Morton shareholders.

The spinoff record and distribution dates are subject to the the approval of the exchange offer by more than 90 percent Autoliv AB common stockholders. That offer is due to expire Thursday, the company said.
Completion of the exchange offer is the remaining condition to the Morton Automotive Safety Products-Autoliv combination.
The spinoff will be completed on the day prior to the completion of the Morton Automotive Safety Products-Autoliv combination, expected to be May 1, Morton said.
Morton said it declared a quarterly dividend of $0.12 per common share, payable on June 9, 1997 to shareholders of record on May 27, 1997.
This amount, combined with the expected dividend to be declared by Autoliv, will result in a total dividend at or above what the shareholders had been receiving.
Out of the 140.6 million shares entitled to vote, the vote for the spinoff was 98.1 million in favor, 400,000 opposed, and 800,000 abstaining.

The vote for the combination was 98.0 million in favor, 400,000 opposed, and 900,000 abstaining. About 71 percent of the company's shareholders were represented either in person or by proxy at the meeting.
The "new" Morton International will be named Morton International Inc and will be listed on the New York and Chicago stock exchanges under the symbol MII.
Autoliv Inc will be listed on the New York exchange under the symbol ALV.
